tagline.text: An autumn festival in Virac marking the founding of Catanduanes province

location.label: Location
location.text: Virac, the provincial capital of Catanduanes; Puraran Beach is in Baras

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~4,000 (per person per day, rough estimate for lodging, meals and local transport; airfare and ferry not included)

children.text: Catandungan celebrates Catanduanes becoming a separate province. Provincial foundation day falls on October 26. The parade and street dances take place in the capital, Virac. Check the separate schedule for surfing competitions at Puraran Beach in Baras.

Catanduanes is an island province standing alone in the sea on the eastern side of the Bicol region. At the 2024 census the province had about 261,000 residents and its capital, Virac, about 75,000. The province is called the "Abaca Capital of the Philippines" because it produces so much abaca fiber, and Wikipedia says its farmers produced about 40 percent of the country's abaca fiber in 2015. The island is open to the Philippine Sea and is often hit by typhoons; the same source says the province has been struck by three super typhoons in the last two decades.
Catandungan refers to island residents.
Republic Act No. 11139
set October 26 as the special holiday for Catanduanes foundation day. The province announces individual event dates each year.

The main program features a street parade, traditional dances and stage performances. Pantomina is a Bicol courtship dance, with costumes and rhythms varying by team. Virac and Baras are separate stops. Check whether a surfing competition appears on your dates.
The
Philippine Information Agency report
confirms the 81st anniversary ran October 26–28, 2026. The Tourism Promotions Board calendar lists October 20–24. Book using the local program for the year you travel.
This dance, said to resemble a rooster and hen's courtship, is the festival's signature program. A Pantomina contest was held on
October 25
in 2023. Each village team has different costumes and moves, which makes comparing them fun, and the contest place and time should be confirmed each year through local announcements.
The
2026 parade route
ran on October 27 from Imelda Boulevard in Concepcion through central Virac to the Provincial Capitol Grounds. Check the start and finish before choosing a viewing spot.

blocks.title: Around the Virac Heroes Memorial Fountain

children.text: The area around the Virac Heroes Memorial Fountain downtown is described as the center of the festival. Beauty pageants, sports games, exhibitions and tournaments were reportedly held around here. If your lodging is downtown, it is easy to get around on foot.

Puraran Beach is in the village of Baras and is called Majestic Wave Beach. Its waves form barrels and are described as suitable for both beginners and advanced surfers, and Wikipedia gives the surfing season as
July–October
. A surfing competition is held during the festival, with side events such as frisbee and wall climbing. Some guides say a surfing cup is held first, in the first week of October.

blocks.title: Virac Cathedral and the thanksgiving Mass

children.text: Virac Cathedral celebrates its parish feast on
December 8
. Thanksgiving Mass and the procession during the October anniversary have their own dates in that edition’s program.
Nahulugan Falls is a three-tiered waterfall in
San Pedro, Gigmoto
. Allow separate overland travel from Puraran in Baras. For a shorter trip from Virac, visit Bato Church.

Abaca (Manila hemp), tied to the island's name, is the province's symbol. During the festival an agro-industrial fair presenting local products is said to be held. Check locally for specific food and prices.

items.title: Two-day festival route
items.subtitle: Virac city events and a look at Puraran surfing

children.text: If the thanksgiving Mass time at Virac Cathedral has been announced, go early and look around the church inside and out.
If a parade runs that day, choose a spot near Imelda Boulevard or the Provincial Capitol. This is the 2026 route example. Check traffic restrictions for your year.
Have lunch at a restaurant in town and browse the market and fair booths.
If the Pantomina contest or a street dance program is on, take a spot.
Watch an evening stage event or a beauty pageant, then return to your lodging.
On the morning of day two, go by car or motorcycle to Puraran Beach to watch the surfing competition or the waves.
The distance and time from Virac to Puraran vary a lot with road conditions, so check locally. In a typhoon, roads and ferries may be cut off.

items.title: Three-day extended route
items.subtitle: The festival plus the island's waterfall and churches

children.text: Arrive on day one, settle into your lodging and look around the city and the event venues.
On the morning of day two, watch the parade and the Pantomina contest, then walk a nearby church and the coast in the afternoon.
On day three, choose Puraran Beach in Baras or Nahulugan Falls in Gigmoto. If visiting both, confirm road travel times and the return ride to Virac.
Reach Nahulugan Falls overland from San Pedro. After heavy rain, check road conditions and access on foot.
The
Catanduanes transport guide
lists the Cebu Pacific nonstop from Manila to Virac at about
1 hour
. Check operating days and flight status with the airline.
Seats fill quickly during the festival, so book early.
The
Regina Shipping booking page
lists Tabaco to San Andres from
one way. The October 2026 fare guide lists air-conditioned seats at
. Allow for onward road transport to Virac.
There are also ferries direct to Virac Port. An earlier Silangan guide lists
ordinary and
air-conditioned. If booking your Manila bus and ferry separately, allow time between the Tabaco bus stop and the port.
Ferries may be canceled in typhoon season, so leave extra room in your return plan.
Tricycles are the main transport in Virac, and jeepneys and buses serve the other municipalities.
Farther places such as Puraran are often reached by hired car, van or motorcycle. Negotiate the fare locally.
Provincial foundation day is October 26. The
Civil Service Commission advisory
confirms the 2026 parade on October 27. Set your stay in Virac after checking the separate parade and surfing dates.
Typhoons are said to be common in
July–October
, so for an October trip it is safer to check the forecast often and choose bookings that can be changed for flights and ferries.

Happy Island Inn
is in San Vicente, Virac, and offers pickup inquiries. For the parade, check access to central Virac. For surfing, look at lodging near Puraran in Baras and book your return ride.

You can eat well in downtown restaurants and the market, with local dishes and seafood as the mainstay. During the festival, street stalls and temporary food booths multiply, so eat where you can see hygiene and prices for yourself. Local specialties are introduced at the local fair.
October is the tail end of typhoon season, so check the forecast often and choose bookings that can be changed.
Parades and contests take place at midday, so bring a hat, sunscreen, water and a raincoat.
Lodging within walking distance is convenient in Virac.
Puraran is a long way, so leave early in the morning and allow plenty of time to get back.
Bring plenty of cash. Markets and tricycles generally take cash.
In churches, cover your shoulders and knees and avoid taking photos during Mass.
Schedules can change, so check the provincial government's official page or social media announcements once more the day before.
Phone signal may be weak in places, so save maps and bookings in advance.
October is a time when typhoons can reach Catanduanes. If flights and ferries stop, you could be stuck for days, so leave extra room in your return plan.
Event schedules and the stated starting year differ by source, so the dates in this guide are examples from past editions. Check the latest announcements.
During the festival, lodging and airfare fill quickly and prices can rise.
The big waves at Puraran can be dangerous for beginners, so mostly watch, or hire an instructor.
San Andres and Virac are separate arrival ports. Check the operator’s schedule and weather notices on the day you sail.
In crowded parades, watch for pickpockets and keep valuables in front of you.
You can combine the festival with the whole island's waterfalls, beaches and churches.
